title: Exit-value forward-NOI-growth timing asymmetry between the two study engines
evidence: Independent quantified reproduction (audit/EXIT_VALUE_AUDIT.md): with rentGrowthRate=0 the two conventions are mathematically identical (masks the issue in the current RE-GOLD-002 fixture); with rentGrowthRate=0.03 (the land study's own default value) the two conventions diverge by +3.00% in sale value (SAR 7,167,852 on the RE-GOLD-002 input set), which flows through to a different npv/irr and could flip criterion c4 near a marginal threshold
reproduction: Set building study rentGrowthRate > 0 (e.g. 0.03) and compare sale value computed via same-year NOI (line 202: noiYear/marketCapRate) against a land-style forward-growth convention (noiYear*(1+rentGrowthRate)/marketCapRate) using the identical input set -- see audit/EXIT_VALUE_AUDIT.md for the exact reproduction script and numbers
impact: Silent recommendation-affecting discrepancy for any building study with nonzero rent growth -- currently invisible because the only golden fixture (RE-GOLD-002) happens to use 0% growth as its default | RESOLVED (D4): Land Development standardized on Convention A (Direct Cap) to match Existing Building -- forwardNOI growth step removed (src/engines/valuation/land-development.js, 2 lines). Existing Building confirmed untouched (md5sum identical). Decision made via neutral DECISION-DEF-001/DEF-001-DECISION-BRIEF.md (3 options presented, no recommendation). 6 fields updated in local RE-GOLD-001 fixtures with audit trail; verdict/criteria unchanged in both known fixtures. Verified: run_triple_path.js modularVsGold=0, run_dual_path.js 0 unexpected mismatches (12 expected DEF-001 divergences documented), tests/defects/def001_decision_verification.js 4/4 PASS. | SUPERSEDED FINAL RESOLUTION: prior D4 Direct-Cap decision was superseded after read-only verification (D5) found it did not match the required Forward NOI semantic. D6 executed the corrected decision: BOTH studies now use forwardNOI = noiYear*(1+rentGrowthRate); saleValue/exitValue = forwardNOI/capRate. Existing Building's own engine was modified for the first time in this remediation (2 lines) to add the previously-absent growth step. Verified: terminal/NOI_N ratio = 1.0300 exactly (was 1.0000 pre-fix), implied saleValue = 246,096,265.01 = expected forward value to the cent. Permanent executable test added: tests/characterization/run_cov001_forward_noi.js (4/4 PASS, non-zero growth + holdPeriod>1, independent of any fixture).
recommended_fix_phase: P1 -- must be preserved/characterized during Rebase (add a non-zero-growth building test case to the characterization suite BEFORE any refactor, so REBASE can prove whether the eventual unified engine intentionally picks one convention or preserves both per study type; do not silently harmonize without a product decision)

title: Out-of-range percentage inputs silently accepted by engine; UI warning is cosmetic only

evidence: Executed adversarial test (audit/evidence/adversarial-input-results.json): occupancyRate=1.5 (150%) on the RE-GOLD-002 input set inflates grossRentalIncome from 14,040,000 to 21,060,000 (+50%) and produces a FULL 5/5 'يوصى بالشراء' recommendation with zero NaN/Infinity and no error surfaced
reproduction: Set building occupancy to 150% (or land occupancy likewise) via the UI percentage field; rangeWarning displays an orange advisory but the value flows unmodified into the income calculation and recommendation
impact: A physically impossible input produces a confident maximum-strength BUY recommendation on inflated income. Highest-risk finding of this wave because output looks fully valid (no NaN marker, no error) while being economically nonsensical. | RESOLVED (D1): occupancyRate constrained to [0,1] at the centralized calculateInvestmentCase boundary (src/validation/numeric-safety.js). Sensitivity analysis's own perturbation logic separately bounded (boundedOccupancyValue in App.jsx) with explicit requestedValue/effectiveValue/boundaryLimited metadata -- occupancy sensitivity dimension preserved, never fed >100% to the engine. Verified: 11/11 engine rejection matrix, 5/5 SENS-OCC boundary tests, real-browser E2E (150% input -> visible validation banner, no crash, app recovers on valid input).
recommended_fix_phase: P1 -- characterize before Rebase (capture current unclamped behavior in a test so the Rebase engine boundary can add validation deliberately rather than accidentally changing existing numbers)

title: NaN/Infinity inputs propagate silently through the entire result object while still emitting a confident recommendation verdict
source_location: platform-source.jsx: NumField/PercentField onChange handler (lines 474-478, 496-500) -- isNaN(parsed) guard does not reject Infinity
evidence: Executed adversarial test (audit/evidence/adversarial-input-results.json): rentPerSqm=Infinity yields 16 NaN + 1 Infinity fields with a fully-rendered confident Arabic verdict, no error surfaced. Separately verified: JSON.stringify({rentPerSqm:Infinity}) serializes to {"rentPerSqm":null} -- Saved Deals path confirmed SAFE, not a corruption vector.
reproduction: AUTHORITATIVE REPRODUCTION = UI_INFINITY_PATH. Type or paste >=309 consecutive digits into any NumField/PercentField numeric input (e.g. 'سعر المبنى'). The regex /[^\d.\-]/g preserves digits, parseFloat() yields Infinity, and isNaN(Infinity)===false so the guard does not reject it. No devtools, no storage tampering required. DEF_003_PREVIOUS_SAVED_DEAL_CLAIM = SUPERSEDED -- an earlier pass in this session incorrectly hypothesized a corrupted-saved-deal path; that hypothesis was tested and disproven (JSON.stringify converts Infinity/NaN to null on save, null then behaves as 0 downstream, not as corruption) -- retracted, not restored here.
impact: User sees a fully-rendered Arabic verdict and dashboard with NaN in individual metric rows but no explicit invalid-input state. The recommendation seal renders as if authoritative, reachable through ordinary keyboard/paste input. | RESOLVED (D1): Number.isFinite() validation (not isNaN(), which the original defect exploited) at the same centralized boundary rejects Infinity/-Infinity/NaN for every numeric field. A critical React crash bug was discovered and fixed during remediation (useMemo previously let ValidationError escape uncaught, freezing the app) -- last-known-valid result now retained via useRef with a visible error banner. Verified: 7/7 rejection cases, real-browser E2E with 320-digit input producing Infinity -- banner shown, 0 page errors, app remains responsive.
recommended_fix_phase: P1 -- characterize before Rebase; add Number.isFinite() guard at the typed-engine boundary during Rebase. Note the fix belongs in NumField's onChange guard (line 477) and/or the engine contract, not in the persistence layer, which was cleared by this analysis.

title: maxPaybackThreshold=0 produces a silent maxJustifiedPrice of 0 via 1/0=Infinity
source_location: platform-source.jsx line 210: NOI / Math.max(inp.minYieldThreshold, 1 / inp.maxPaybackThreshold); NumField call site at line 1183 has min={1}
evidence: Executed test: with maxPaybackThreshold=0 supplied directly to calcExistingBuilding (bypassing the UI), 1/0 evaluates to Infinity, Math.max picks Infinity, NOI/Infinity=0 -- the 'أعلى سعر شراء يحقق المعايير' guidance metric displays 0 SAR with no warning. Direct verification of the NumField call site (line 1183) confirms min={1} IS set, and NumField's onChange applies Math.max(min, parsed) (line 478) -- ordinary UI typing cannot produce 0 for this field; any value below 1 is silently clamped up to 1 before reaching state.
reproduction: CORRECTED: the earlier reproduction claim ("set the field to 0 via the building input panel") was WRONG and is retracted here, not restored -- min={1} blocks ordinary UI entry. Realistic non-devtools reproduction path: a saved-deal record with maxPaybackThreshold<=0 (edited outside the app, or a legacy/malformed persisted record), loaded via loadDeal, which spreads record.inputs directly over defaults with NO min-value re-validation on load (confirmed: loadDeal, lines 1568-1583, contains no clamping logic -- the min={1} constraint exists only inside NumField's onChange handler, not as a load-time or engine-level invariant).
impact: Displays a meaningless 0 SAR maximum-justified-price as investment guidance. Low severity: does not affect the verdict criteria; requires a tampered/legacy saved-deal record or direct engine invocation, not ordinary use. | RESOLVED (D2): maxPaybackThreshold constrained to strictly >0 (STRICTLY_POSITIVE_DIVISOR_FIELDS in the same centralized validator), applied identically to both studies (confirmed shared field name). Negative values (previously producing a plausible-looking but meaningless positive price with zero error indication -- a worse case than the originally-documented zero) are now also rejected. Verified: direct engine rejection for both studies and both zero/negative cases, and a real corrupted-saved-deal record injected via the actual BrowserLocalStorageProvider triggering the validation banner with zero code changes beyond the shared D1 recovery mechanism.

title: Zero purchase price produces an economically inverted (worse) score than a fairly-priced building
source_location: platform-source.jsx lines 182-183 (netYieldOnPrice / paybackOnPrice divide-by-zero guards return 0) and line 237 (criterion c1)
evidence: Executed comparison: buildingPrice=0 -> netYieldOnPrice=0, paybackOnPrice=0, c1=false (0 >= minYieldThreshold is false), c2=true, verdict='يوصى بالشراء بشروط' 4/5; a fairly-priced building scores 5/5. A free asset therefore scores WORSE than a priced one.
reproduction: Set 'سعر المبنى' to 0 and compare the recommendation seal against the RE-GOLD-002 default price
impact: Technical artifact of the divide-by-zero protection (guard returns 0, which then fails the >= yield threshold) rather than an economic model error. A zero purchase price is outside the supported product domain (a real acquisition study always has a price), so no user-facing decision is realistically affected.
recommended_fix_phase: P3 -- post-Rebase; revisit only if zero/nominal-price scenarios (gift, inheritance, intra-group transfer) become a supported product use case
